input.content:
## Plain English

When the Fresha or Square integration feature is turned off in config, a "gatekeeper" in the observer already stops jobs from being dispatched at all — they never enter the queue. But the jobs themselves had a second identical gatekeeper that ran *inside* the queue worker after the job was already dequeued. That second gatekeeper was never triggered under normal conditions, and in the rare case where the feature flag changed mid-flight, it would silently discard the work with no log entry. We removed the in-job gatekeeper and left only the observer gatekeeper, which is the right place for this control.

## Technical Summary

Removed the `config('partna.features.fresha_sync')` early-return from `PushServiceToFreshaJob::handle()` (app/Jobs/Fresha/PushServiceToFreshaJob.php) and the equivalent `config('partna.features.square_sync')` guard from `PushServiceToSquareJob::handle()` (app/Jobs/Square/PushServiceToSquareJob.php). The canonical flag gates remain in `ServiceObserver::shouldDispatchFreshaSync()` and `shouldDispatchSquareSync()`. Two test cases in `tests/Feature/FeatureFlags/SyncJobsGatedTest.php` that tested the now-removed job-level behaviour were deleted; their imports were cleaned up accordingly. Observer-level gating is already fully covered by `tests/Feature/FeatureFlags/ServiceObserverSyncGatedTest.php`. The `SyncSquareCatalogDeltaJob` and `SyncFreshaCatalogDeltaJob` tests (also in `SyncJobsGatedTest.php`) were untouched — those scheduled jobs legitimately own their own flag guards since they have no observer gatekeeper.

## Decisions Made

- Deleted the two failing test cases rather than updating them: the tests were asserting behaviour that was intentionally removed; the observer-level equivalent tests already existed in `ServiceObserverSyncGatedTest.php`, so there was nothing to replace them with that wasn't already covered.
- Did not touch `SyncSquareCatalogDeltaJob` or `SyncFreshaCatalogDeltaJob`: these scheduled/polling jobs have no observer gatekeeper, so their job-level flag guard is the correct and only gate — the audit item correctly scoped only the `PushService*` jobs.

## Notes

The `OpenInviteTest` suite was already failing (AWS SDK S3 error on PutObjectCopy) before this change and is unrelated. The two pre-existing failures persisted in the full test run; all other tests pass.
